metas.name: Bernie
metas.description: Based on a true story: a beloved small-town Texas mortician kills a hated widow, and the town would rather he got away with it. Richard Linklater plays it completely straight.

metas.name: The Lobster
metas.description: Yorgos Lanthimos's satire in which single people get 45 days to find a partner or be turned into animals. Everyone delivers absurd cruelty in a flat monotone.

metas.name: Happiness
metas.description: Todd Solondz's interlocking portrait of suburban New Jersey, where ordinary people hide monstrous secrets. It is unbearably deadpan.

metas.name: The Art of Self-Defense
metas.description: A timid accountant joins a karate dojo that turns out to be a cult of toxic masculinity. Bone-dry comedy that escalates into real violence.

metas.name: Force Majeure
metas.description: A father runs from an avalanche and leaves his family behind, and the rest of their ski holiday turns into a quiet trial. Ruben Östlund's precise, excruciating comedy.

metas.name: Kinds of Kindness
metas.description: Yorgos Lanthimos's three-part film about people who give up everything to please those who control them. Cruel, strange and deadpan throughout.

metas.name: Fargo
metas.description: The Coen brothers' crime story about a car salesman whose plan to have his wife kidnapped falls apart. Murder plays out against Minnesota politeness.

metas.name: To Die For
metas.description: Nicole Kidman plays a small-town weather girl who will do anything to get on TV, including talking teenagers into murder. A sly satire played cool.

metas.name: World's Greatest Dad
metas.description: After his awful son dies in an embarrassing accident, a failed writer fakes a suicide note, and the whole school embraces the lie. Bobcat Goldthwait's pitch-black comedy.

metas.name: Sightseers
metas.description: A mild British couple on a caravan holiday start killing anyone who annoys them. Ben Wheatley plays the murders as small domestic matters.
